paragraphs.dominant_move: sports and data coverage -> annual game graphs
coach-player separation -> likelihood, optimization, and career list
stakeholder coach question -> scope and output
annual network and centrality -> team ranking
skill separation and objective -> optimizer and historical aggregation

global_organization_chain: The summary compresses the sport scope, yearly network route, eigenvector ranking, coach-player separation, optimization, and century ranking.
The public explainer, technical title, and contents convert the broad coach question into data, network, separation, optimization, ranking, and testing sections.
The paper restates the all-time coach task and presents a six-step route from annual game graphs to historical coach ranking.
The assumptions fix annual team skill, multiplicative team composition, and the player-gap condition under which coaching affects a result.
The data section describes game-result collection, coach matching, standardized names, and sport-specific coverage limits.
A weighted directed graph encodes annual wins, repeated meetings, and score margins before any team ranking is calculated.
The paper contrasts degree, betweenness, closeness, and eigenvector centrality, then validates the chosen ranking against published polls.
Team skill is factorized into coach and player skill, then player gaps damp coach effect and determine the margin-likelihood expression.
The joint likelihood is converted to a squared objective, rejected methods are documented, and Powell search is retained for yearly coach vectors.
Annual top-five appearances are normalized by active years to produce the final cross-century coach lists.
Two single-game perturbations, strengths, and computational limitations bound the claimed robustness of the ranking.
The conclusion restates the graph-to-ranking route and the references expose the web and method dependencies needed to reproduce it.
Only after the positive language, organization, model, result, and visual chains are complete does the final pass record notation, identifiability, solver, sensitivity, and reproducibility warnings.

main_argument_chains.claim: Annual team comparison becomes more opponent-aware when winner-to-loser game records are encoded as weighted directed graphs and scored by eigenvector centrality.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the team score only with the stated graph orientation, sport-year coverage, and centrality convergence conditions.

main_argument_chains.claim: Coach ranking is made operational by factorizing team skill, damping coach differences by player gaps, and fitting a margin likelihood across annual games.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not interpret separate coach skill as identified without an explicit normalization and data-generating contract.

main_argument_chains.claim: A yearly coach vector is selected only after the source compares attempted solvers and retains Powell's method for its observed cost reduction.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Run documented multi-start diagnostics before treating a selected local search as a stable optimum.

main_argument_chains.claim: The all-time tables follow from annual top-five appearances divided by active years, then receive a limited single-game sensitivity check.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Publish rank uncertainty and coverage limits rather than treating two directed changes as general robustness.

warnings.warning: The walk-series term visibly changes the exponent sign convention; verify whether the final exponent should remain negative before implementation.
The team-skill product does not state the normalization needed to identify coach and player skill separately.
The damped-effect expression needs a calibrated alpha and an explicit regime for the approximation of similarly matched players.
The probability expression uses italic multiword quantities and lacks a complete parameter, normalization, and domain specification.
The joint product is asserted without a complete normalization or dependence contract across games.
The likelihood-to-objective equivalence is asserted after algebra; reconstruct the constants and objective domain before numerical reuse.
The active-years-normalized top-five frequency remains conditional on top-five thresholding, sport coverage, and the annual optimizer.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: A two-team directed-edge illustration explains the winner-to-loser encoding before the technical paper begins.
The public explainer displays the final top-five names for the three sports.
The contents exposes the source sequence from data and network ranking to separation, optimization, ranking, testing, and conclusion.
The network diagram shows nodes as teams and edges as games, with conference clustering visible.
The centrality definition, matrix eigenvector relation, and walk series make the selected team-ranking mechanism inspectable.
The three-column top-ten table compares eigenvector centrality with AP and USA Today rankings.
Node size and darkness encode relative eigenvector centrality in the complete seasonal network.
The centered product equation connects team skill to coach and player skill.
Two margin-probability sketches and the player-gap damping expression motivate when coach effect is used.
The annual product and squared objective make the optimization handoff visible.
Three widely separated yearly top-three lists serve as the source's selected-solver output.
The career-frequency ratio and three-sport table translate annual output into the final decision artifact.
The two perturbation cases connect one changed game to score and rank response.
